title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming continued through 2025 with iterative point releases — Haiku 4.5 (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, and Opus 4.7, followed by Opus 4.8 in early 2026. Each point release brought incremental gains in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction-following precision without changing the three-tier structure.

**Correction (August 2026):** an earlier version of this page listed Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.7 as the "current" models. They have since been superseded — see the Claude 5 Family section below for the current lineup and model IDs.

---

## Claude 5 Family — a Mythos-Class Tier Arrives (June–July 2026)

Anthropic shipped four new models in about eight weeks, introducing a new top tier above Opus for the first time:

- **Claude Sonnet 5** (`claude-sonnet-5`) — released June 30, 2026. A drop-in upgrade for Sonnet 4.6 with **adaptive thinking on by default**, a 1M-token context window (the default and only size — no smaller variant), 128K max output tokens, and a new tokenizer that produces roughly 30% more tokens than Sonnet 4.6's for the same text. Scores 85.2% on SWE-bench Verified and 80.4% on Terminal-Bench. Priced at $3/$15 per million input/output tokens ($2/$10 introductory through August 31, 2026; standard pricing applies from September 1). Manual extended thinking (`budget_tokens`) is removed and now returns a 400 error — use adaptive thinking with the effort parameter instead.
- **Claude Fable 5** (`claude-fable-5`) — released June 9, 2026 (briefly suspended June 12–30 under U.S. export controls, restored globally July 1). The first model in a new **"Mythos-class"** tier sitting above Opus — Anthropic's most capable public model to date, state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks. A safeguards-lifted twin, **Claude Mythos 5**, is available only through a limited program for infrastructure providers and vetted cybersecurity researchers. Fable 5 is priced at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens.
- **Claude Opus 5** (`claude-opus-5`) — released July 24, 2026. A faster, roughly-half-the-price alternative that approaches Fable 5's results on many coding and knowledge-work benchmarks — SOTA on Frontier-Bench, 3x the next-best model on ARC-AGI 3, within 0.5% of Fable 5 on CursorBench — while keeping Opus 4.8's $5/$25 per million token pricing. Became the new default model on Claude Max and the strongest model available on Claude Pro.
- **Claude Haiku 4.5** (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) — still the fastest/cheapest tier; unlike the three 2026 flagships it retains a 200K-token context window rather than 1M.

All three 2026 flagships (Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5) share two behavior changes from their 4.x predecessors: **effort controls** (a low/medium/high/max parameter trading capability for latency and cost, replacing manual `budget_tokens` thinking) and rejection of non-default `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` values (guide behavior via system prompt instead). See the Claude Code page for how effort controls and adaptive thinking show up in the CLI.

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K → 1M tokens (Sonnet 5, Opus 5, and Fable 5 all default to 1M; Haiku 4.5 remains at 200K)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → Four tiers with the June 2026 addition of the Mythos-class Fable/Mythos tier above Opus
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing (Opus 5 explicitly targets ~half of Fable 5's cost)
- **Thinking control:** Manual `budget_tokens` extended thinking has been fully retired across the 2026 flagship lineup in favor of adaptive thinking plus an explicit effort parameter
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, and integration with external systems
